Description: Rapid decarbonization with immediate policy action. Consistent with Paris Agreement 1.5C target. Strong carbon pricing, rapid renewable scaling, phase-out of fossil fuels by 2040-2050.
Key_Assumptions: Rapid coal phase-out (2025-2030), 5% annual renewables growth, carbon pricing drives transition, net-zero by 2050 mandatory, technology costs fall 60% by 2050

Description: Current policies trajectory with gradual improvements. Achieves 2C goal with delayed action. Moderate carbon pricing, mixed policy support, technology gradual deployment.
Key_Assumptions: Coal phase-out 2035-2045, 3% annual renewables growth, carbon pricing moderate (50-100), net-zero by 2070, slower technology cost curves

Description: Limited climate action beyond current pledges. Market forces drive some change but insufficient. Minimal carbon pricing, slow renewable deployment, fossil fuels persist.
Key_Assumptions: Coal continues for baseload (phase-out only post-2050), 1.5% annual renewables growth, weak carbon pricing (10-40), net-zero not committed, technology costs fall only 20-30%

Description: Achieves 1.5C but through delayed and accelerated action. Higher transition costs. Policy delayed until 2028-2030 then rapid phase-out.
Key_Assumptions: Late coal phase-out (2025-2030 continued, then rapid 2030-2040), 8% annual renewables growth post-2031, extreme carbon pricing 2030+ (200-500), acceleration costs higher

Description: Uneven transition: rapid in some sectors (renewable, EVs), slow in others (aviation, agriculture, shipping). Creates pockets of stranded assets and transition winners/losers.
Key_Assumptions: Coal phase-out 2035-2045 (but uneven: power 2035, industry 2045), sectoral carbon pricing (renewables 50, fossil 200), net-zero by 2065, technology divergence by sector
